# Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects — facts

> Source-anchored units about Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects: 15 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 15 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] Finout's MongoDB integration page labels the integration Beta and says it imports daily line-item billing data through a service account with read-only billing access. This is vendor-documented support for bringing Atlas project and cluster costs into Finout's virtual-tag allocation layer. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29) — https://www.finout.io/mongodb · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects

## How it works

- [statement] Vantage and Finout document splitting shared costs across virtual-tag values using business metrics or telemetry. These methods provide an allocation basis when a resource-level owner does not identify all consumers; the selected metric is an attribution proxy, not proof of each consumer's exact cost causation. (medium confidence) — https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-dynamic-cost-allocation · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects · also: https://docs.finout.io/user-guide/inform/shared-cost-reallocation

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Finout advertises Atlas billing ingestion and Virtual Tags for team/service allocation; its separate shared-cost documentation describes telemetry weighting and customized percentages totaling 100%. Applying those general mechanisms to an Atlas shared-cost pool is an integration inference, not an Atlas-specific worked example in the reviewed pages. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.finout.io/mongodb · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects · also: https://docs.finout.io/user-guide/inform/shared-cost-reallocation
- [statement] Vantage's dynamic-allocation documentation warns that a business metric missing for a date will not match that day's costs. It recommends a lower-priority matching value when unmatched costs need a tag assignment. Its claim of allocating 100% therefore requires attention to metric coverage and fallback rules. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-07-29) — https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-dynamic-cost-allocation · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects
- [statement] Vantage's July 2024 launch documentation describes dynamic allocation using an input cost or labeled business metric, a destination tag key, and an output cost to split. For daily allocation, a tag value responsible for 56% of the input receives 56% of the selected output cost. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-07-29) — https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-dynamic-cost-allocation · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects
- [statement] Finout documents two shared-cost strategies: telemetry-based reallocation using indicators such as bytes, query length, or business KPIs; and customized percentages, including an equal split or unequal agreed shares totaling 100%. Its documentation states that virtual tags with reallocation are unavailable in raw data. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://docs.finout.io/user-guide/inform/shared-cost-reallocation · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Atlas invoice CSV and Admin API resource tags reflect tag configuration when the export is generated or the API is invoked; changes during the billing cycle appear as the latest configuration. Historical cost ownership cannot be inferred from these tags alone. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/billing.md · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects
- [statement] A commenter in the Unclear charges on Atlas discussion reported difficulty identifying which user contributed to costs within one cluster. This is anecdotal evidence of an attribution problem, not proof of a current Atlas limitation. (low confidence) — https://www.reddit.com/r/mongodb/comments/14msseo/ · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Shared-cost allocation can use measured or proxy weights rather than equal shares: Finout documents external telemetry and business KPIs, while Vantage documents proportions derived from other costs or business metrics. This is a general allocation method, not proof of native Atlas per-tenant metering. (high confidence) — https://docs.finout.io/user-guide/inform/shared-cost-reallocation · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects · also: https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-dynamic-cost-allocation
- [statement] Vantage advertises allocation of MongoDB costs including shared clusters. Its dynamic-allocation announcement describes splitting any ingested cost among virtual-tag values using proportions from another cost or business metric; these are vendor capability statements rather than independent performance evidence. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-07-29) — https://www.vantage.sh/integrations/mongodb · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects · also: https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-dynamic-cost-allocation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas configures billing at organization level, with shared billing settings and payment method across projects; project-level cost attribution therefore does not create a separate payment arrangement for each project. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/ · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects · also: https://www.finout.io/mongodb
- [statement] Atlas supports deployment resource tags to categorize costs beyond the default invoice breakdown. Finout also documents mapping imported Atlas billing data by project, cluster, service, and Atlas resource tags. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/billing.md · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects · also: https://www.finout.io/mongodb
- [statement] Atlas documents that its Summary By Project table excludes subscription charges. A project usage subtotal alone therefore does not reconcile the entire organizational invoice. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/ · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects
- [statement] Vantage’s February 2023 integration announcement describes reading Atlas invoice line items and filtering by organization and project, with grouping by cluster and tag. It documents reporting inputs; it does not demonstrate an automatic allocation of database-user consumption. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-02-01) — https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-mongodb-atlas-costs · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects
- [statement] Vantage's Atlas integration ingests invoice line items through the Invoices API, supports project-level filtering, and documents grouping costs by service, cluster, and tag. Its launch documentation also describes combining Atlas project costs with related infrastructure-provider costs in one report. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-02-01) — https://www.vantage.sh/blog/vantage-launches-mongodb-atlas-costs · keywords: Shared-cost splitting for Atlas projects
